citation: Kirson ED et al. Disruption of Cancer Cell Replication by Alternating Electric Fields
model_or_population: in vitro and animal tumor models
mechanism_or_question: Initial biological effect and frequency dependence
key_finding: TTFields inhibited tumor-cell growth and selectively affected dividing cells; effects included mitotic spindle disruption and division-associated cell destruction.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Cell growth, mitotic morphology, tumor growth
limitations: Multiple tumor models; early mechanistic study rather than a complete molecular explanation.
notes: Several authors affiliated with NovoCure Ltd.

citation: Gera N et al. Tumor Treating Fields Perturb the Localization of Septins and Cause Aberrant Mitotic Exit
model_or_population: HeLa, MDA-MB-231, HCT116, and MCF-7 cells
key_finding: TTFields disrupted Septin 2/6/7 localization at the anaphase spindle midline and cytokinetic furrow, with membrane blebbing, aberrant mitotic exit, and subsequent cell stress/apoptosis.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Septin localization, mitotic progression, membrane blebbing, apoptosis
limitations: Cell-line study; septin perturbation supports but does not prove a single direct molecular target.
notes: NovoCure funding/training support disclosed; research reported as independently conducted.

citation: Karanam NK et al. Tumor-treating fields elicit a conditional vulnerability to ionizing radiation via the downregulation of BRCA1 signaling and reduced DNA double-strand break repair capacity in non-small cell lung cancer cell lines
key_finding: TTFields altered cell-cycle progression and downregulated BRCA1-pathway genes; exposure increased DNA-damage foci and chromatid aberrations and reduced repair capacity after ionizing radiation.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: G2/M and S-phase populations, DNA-repair foci, chromatid aberrations, cell survival
limitations: Study was performed in NSCLC rather than GBM; combination effects require disease-specific validation.
notes: Original experimental study; funded by NovoCure Ltd.

citation: Giladi M et al. Tumor treating fields delay DNA damage repair following radiation treatment of glioma cells
model_or_population: glioma cell lines with in vitro and in vivo/translational components
mechanism_or_question: Whether TTFields alter radiation-induced DNA damage repair
key_finding: TTFields delayed repair of radiation-induced DNA damage in glioma models, supporting a radiosensitizing mechanism.
limitations: Combination-treatment study; not evidence that DNA-repair interference is the sole monotherapy mechanism.

citation: Voloshin T et al. Tumor Treating Fields Hinder Cancer Cell Motility through Regulation of Microtubule and Actin Dynamics
model_or_population: U-87 MG, A-172, LN-229, LN-18 GBM cells plus A549 and H1299 lung adenocarcinoma cells
mechanism_or_question: Effects on cell migration and cytoskeletal dynamics
key_finding: TTFields perturbed microtubule assembly/directionality, GEF-H1/RhoA/ROCK signaling, actin organization, and focal adhesions, reducing migration/invasion-related phenotypes.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Migration, invasion, cytoskeletal organization, signaling activity
limitations: All authors were NovoCure employees or stockholders; mechanistic relevance to motility is distinct from the canonical mitotic mechanism.

citation: Chen D et al. Tumor Treating Fields dually activate STING and AIM2 inflammasomes to induce adjuvant immunity in glioblastoma
model_or_population: GBM cells and syngeneic mouse GBM models
mechanism_or_question: Potential immunological consequences of TTFields-induced cellular damage
key_finding: TTFields induced micronuclei and activated cGAS-STING and AIM2 pathways, producing inflammatory signaling and antitumor immune memory in mouse models.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Inflammatory signaling, immune memory, tumor control
limitations: Mouse-model findings do not establish clinical immune effects in patients; this is an emerging mechanism rather than the canonical explanation.
notes: Use cautiously when translating mouse immune findings to patients.

citation: Karanam NK et al. Tumor treating fields cause replication stress and interfere with DNA replication fork maintenance: Implications for cancer therapy
model_or_population: cancer cell lines with mechanistic replication assays
key_finding: TTFields reduced replication-fork speed, reduced expression of MCM6/MCM10 and Fanconi-anemia-pathway genes, increased R-loop formation, and created a conditional vulnerability to DNA-damaging or DNA-repair-targeting agents.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Replication-fork speed, newly synthesized DNA length, R-loops, gene expression, combination survival
limitations: The study is not a review and is not GBM-specific; mechanistic links to mitotic disruption were investigated primarily in NSCLC models.
notes: Original experimental study; authors were at UT Southwestern Medical Center.

citation: Kirson ED et al. Alternating electric fields arrest cell proliferation in animal tumor models and human brain tumors
model_or_population: MDA-MB-231, H1299, B16F1, intracranial F-98 glioma, U-118/U-87 glioma cells, and 10 patients with recurrent GBM
mechanism_or_question: Disease relevance, optimal frequency, and translation to brain tumors
key_finding: TTFields inhibited proliferation in tumor models; glioma models showed an optimal frequency around 200 kHz, and the study included intracranial F-98 glioma and a 10-patient recurrent GBM pilot.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Cell proliferation, tumor growth, time to progression, overall survival
limitations: The human component was a small pilot study without randomized control; clinical outcomes should not be treated as definitive efficacy evidence.
notes: NovoCure-affiliated investigators; clinical component used historical comparisons.

citation: Giladi M et al. Mitotic Spindle Disruption by Alternating Electric Fields Leads to Improper Chromosome Segregation and Mitotic Catastrophe in Cancer Cells
model_or_population: Multiple cancer cell lines including U-87 MG and U-118 MG glioblastoma cells
ttfields_context: TTFields at tumor-type relevant frequencies including 200 kHz for GBM lines
mechanism_or_question: Direct evidence for microtubule and spindle disruption
key_finding: TTFields reduced the fraction of polymerized tubulin, impaired mitotic spindle assembly, and produced abnormal chromosome segregation, multinucleation, and caspase-dependent apoptosis; effects depended on cell division rate and exposure duration.
primary_endpoint_or_measure: Polymerized/total tubulin ratio, spindle morphology, chromosome segregation, multinucleation, apoptosis, clonogenic survival
limitations: All authors were affiliated with NovoCure, so independent replication is important; study used established cell lines rather than patient tumors.
